```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Bind the Python env with fiorino BEFORE either torch runtime loads.
# R-torch (brulee) bundles libtorch 2.8.0, so the env must carry a matching
# Python torch: pip install "torch==2.8.0" --index-url \
# https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
reticulate::use_virtualenv("r-reticulate", required = FALSE)
library(panettone)
tictoc::tic.clearlog()
```

## The data

A monthly series with trend plus annual seasonality. We train on `t =
1:138` and hold out `t = 139:150` as the actuals our forecasts compete
against.

```{r data}
set.seed(20261014)
n_train <- 138L
h <- 12L
t_all <- seq_len(n_train + h)
y_all <- sin(2 * pi * t_all / 12) + 0.02 * t_all + rnorm(length(t_all), sd = 0.3)

context <- data.frame(timestamp = seq_len(n_train), target = y_all[seq_len(n_train)])
actual <- y_all[n_train + seq_len(h)]

plot(context$timestamp, context$target, type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "t", ylab = "y", main = "Training data (t = 1:138)")
```

## Shared features

One feature table for all engines — the whole point of the adapter. A
running index plus seasonal encodings (reference-style, no lags, so all
12 horizon rows are knowable at forecast time):

```{r features}
context <- as_ts_frame(context)
future <- make_future_frame(context, h)
feats <- build_features(context, future, default_features(period = 12))
feature_cols <- setdiff(names(feats$train), c("item_id", "timestamp", "target"))
X_train <- feats$train[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE]
y_train <- feats$train$target
X_test <- feats$test[, feature_cols, drop = FALSE]
str(X_train)
```

## TabICL: fit, then predict

```{r tabicl-fit}
tictoc::tic("tabicl fit")
fit_icl <- fit_backend(ts_backend("tabicl", num_estimators = 1L), X_train, y_train)
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r tabicl-predict}
tictoc::tic("tabicl predict")
pred_icl <- predict_backend(fit_icl, X_test, quantiles = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
pred_icl
```

## TabPFN: fit, then predict

```{r tabpfn-fit}
tictoc::tic("tabpfn fit")
fit_pfn <- fit_backend(ts_backend("tabpfn", version = "v3.5", num_estimators = 4L),
                       X_train, y_train)
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r tabpfn-predict}
tictoc::tic("tabpfn predict")
pred_pfn <- predict_backend(fit_pfn, X_test, quantiles = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
pred_pfn
```

## Fiorino: fit, then predict

Fiorino's bucket head models `log1p(y)`, so the backend shifts targets
non-negative on train statistics and inverts after prediction (see
`?fit_backend`). It is point-only — no native quantiles:

```{r fiorino-fit}
tictoc::tic("fiorino fit")
fit_fio <- fit_backend(ts_backend("fiorino", device = "cpu"), X_train, y_train)
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r fiorino-predict}
tictoc::tic("fiorino predict")
pred_fio <- predict_backend(fit_fio, X_test, quantiles = NULL)
tictoc::toc(log = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
pred_fio
```

## Forecasts vs actuals

```{r plot-compare, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
ts <- n_train + seq_len(h)
ylim <- range(actual, pred_icl$.pred, pred_pfn$.pred, pred_fio$.pred)
plot(ts, actual, type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2,
     ylim = ylim, xlab = "t", ylab = "y",
     main = "12-step forecasts vs actuals")
lines(ts, pred_icl$.pred, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
lines(ts, pred_pfn$.pred, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
lines(ts, pred_fio$.pred, col = "tomato", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topleft", c("actual", "tabicl", "tabpfn", "fiorino"),
       col = c("black", "steelblue", "darkgreen", "tomato"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 2, 2), lwd = 2, pch = c(16, NA, NA, NA), bty = "n")
```

## Prediction intervals

Native 80% intervals for the two quantile backends (Fiorino stays
point-only until a residual/conformal layer lands):

```{r plot-intervals, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 2, 1))
iv <- list(tabicl = pred_icl, tabpfn = pred_pfn)
for (eng in names(iv)) {
  p <- iv[[eng]]
  plot(ts, actual, type = "b", pch = 16,
       ylim = range(actual, p$q0.1, p$q0.9),
       xlab = "t", ylab = "y", main = eng)
  polygon(c(ts, rev(ts)), c(p$q0.1, rev(p$q0.9)),
          col = grDevices::adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(ts, p$.pred, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
}
```

## Speed and accuracy

```{r score}
scores <- data.frame(
  engine = c("tabicl", "tabpfn", "fiorino"),
  MAE = round(c(mae(actual, pred_icl$.pred),
                mae(actual, pred_pfn$.pred),
                mae(actual, pred_fio$.pred)), 3)
)
scores
tictoc::tic.log(format = TRUE)
```
